text:
Alex Killorn is 37, a two-time Stanley Cup winner from the Tampa years, and still playing 16 minutes a night for a Ducks team that has lost six of its last ten. He has 5 goals and 11 points in 26 games, which looks like a veteran slowing down until you see the chances.

His own finishing is fine: 5 goals on 5.3 expected (the quality of his shots). The gap is around him. Anaheim has scored 6.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Killorn on the ice, and that kind of shortfall usually swings back. The Ducks also do better at five on five with him out there than without, by about four points of expected-goal share.

Two goals against San Jose on Nov. 25 ended a quiet stretch, and his 1,032 career games before this season are a reminder of how long he's been the useful forward on good teams. Our range puts him around 17 goals by April. On this roster, the version of Killorn that matters is the one who keeps showing up in the right places while the puck refuses to go in for his linemates.
headline: Killorn's points are lagging his play
